newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Unigate, Northern eye flat profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Unigate, Northern eye flat profits.

text.p: British diary and food company's Unigate Plc and Northern Foods Plc are expected to report virtually unchanged profits at the full year, as their dairy divisions suffer from sharply reduced butter fat prices, said analysts.

On average brokers expect Unigate, which reports on Monday, to post pretax, pre-exceptional profits of 126 million stg little changed from the prior year period. They foresee a penny on the total dividend to make 20.2p.
An exceptional charge of 14 million is expected for the cost of integrating Kraft's European margarine and spreads business which includes Vitalite and Golden Churn brands, acquired in August.

At the half year stage Unigate estimated that lower butter and milk powder prices cost it about 4.0 million stg in the first half compared with the same period last year. It made pretax profits in the half year to September 30 of 60.6 million or 0.3 percent higher.

Northern Foods, due to report on Tuesday, is also forecast to post pretax profits of some 126 million little changed from the prior year of 124.2 million. A dividend of 9.3p per share is forecast up from 9.0p last time

For the six months ended September 30, 1996 the company posted a one percent rise in pretax, pre-exceptional profits to 57.8 million. The company said prices on the world commodity markets for butter, skimmed milk and bulk cream were off some 20 percent on last year's levels.
Weakening world demand for dairy products and the rise in sterling against the other major European currencies was not offset by a reduction in Northern's cost of milk.
The company estimated the collapse in commodity prices cost it about 6.0 million stg at the half year stage and analysts say the trend has continued.
Competition in supplying milk to supermarkets remain intense and their price demands are still tough, they said.
"They both will have gone back in their dairy business because butter fat prices have fallen sharply especially in sterling terms," said Michael Bourke, analyst at Panmure Gordon.

Northern and Unigate produce large quantities of semi-skimmed and skimmed liquid milk of which butter fat is a by-product. Northern sells it on while Unigate makes butter from it. With skimmed cream down about 17 pence a litre in price at about 1.16 stg a litre compared with last year's average, much of this 75 litre a year by-product for Northern is ending up on the commodity market.

Northern's profits from dairy are forecast to fall some 30 percent to 43 million although its prepared foods business should offset much of this with a 20 percent increase in profits from products like Marks & Spencer recipe dishes.
